grimoire.title: Wildfire and smoke
grimoire.text: Track AQI and evacuation orders, shelter in place with filtered air above AQI 200, pre-stage transport, protect vulnerable groups, follow official evacuation zones.

grimoire.title: Fire / smoke evacuation
grimoire.text: Pull the alarm, evacuate via nearest stairwell, never elevators, assemble at the muster point, sweep sectors, report missing persons to fire services.

grimoire.title: Flash flood
grimoire.text: Move to higher floors, cut power to flooded areas, never drive through water, stage pumps, track river gauges and official warnings.

grimoire.title: Crowd density emergency
grimoire.text: Stop inflow, open all exits, use calm PA messaging, create relief routes, deploy stewards at choke points; above 5 people per square metre is critical.

grimoire.title: Venue power outage
grimoire.text: Switch to emergency lighting, keep stairwells clear, do not use elevators, account for every attendee by sector, check life-safety systems, coordinate with building management.

grimoire.title: Doctrine: EVACUATE
grimoire.text: Evacuate when the threat is mobile, there is structural compromise, or civilians are in the contact zone (pinned, trapped, exposed). Clear floors top-down and confirm empty.

## How good is the quality of air in San Francisco?
The air quality of San Francisco is rated on average as falling into the “good” bracket of the United States Air Quality Index (US AQI), which describes a level of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) between 0 to 12 μg/m^3.

In the last three years, five of the most destructive California wildfires were in relatively close proximity to San Francisco, greatly impacting the quality of air across the Bay Area.^2 In November 2018, the Camp fire burned 153,336 acres of land and drove San Francisco’s AQI for the month up to 137, putting it into the “unhealthy for sensitive groups” bracket, which poses concern for young children, the elderly and those with a predisposition to respiratory ailments.

# When will the wildfire smoke clear out of the SF Bay Area?
The EPA's AirNow map showed "unhealthy" air quality levels in parts of the San Francisco Bay Area on Aug. 30, 2023.

### Don't let Google decide who you trust.
**Aug. 30, 1:15 p.m.**Some parts of the Bay Area had air-quality levels in the red “unhealthy” range on Wednesday afternoon, according to the Environmental Protection Agency’s AirNow website, which tracks air-quality levels across the country. At this level, the agency recommends that people reduce activity or go indoors.

The unhealthy air was predominantly in the North Bay, including Santa Rosa and Petaluma, as of 1 p.m. Parts of the East Bay had air quality at the orange “unhealthy for sensitive groups” level, while the levels were moderate in San Francisco.

The EPA measures air quality with an Air Quality Index that has six levels: good, moderate, unhealthy for sensitive groups, unhealthy, very unhealthy and hazardous.

# Bay Area Air Quality Map, Forecast as San Francisco Shrouded in Smoke
San Francisco currently ranks among the worst places for air quality as smoke from wildfires in northern California and Oregon descends on the Bay Area.

The city has the seventh most polluted air among regions of the world, behind Lahore in Pakistan and Jakarta in Indonesia, according to IQAir, a monitoring company. While pollution is likely to play a role in San Francisco's poor air quality, tracking data shows it has gone from being deemed "good" on Monday to nine times the annual pollutant guideline set by the World Health Organization as of Tuesday.

# Bay Area air quality today: Maps show San Francisco AQI impacted by wildfire smoke
The Bay Area Air Quality Management District issued an air quality advisory Tuesday that lasts through Wednesday as smoke from the wildfires is causing air quality to reach "high-moderate" on the EPA's Air Quality Index.

According to the advisory, smoky and hazy skies may be visible and the smell of smoke is possible, but pollutant levels are not expected to exceed the national 24-hour health standard. The advisory also noted there is no Spare the Air Alert in effect.
San Francisco was ranked as the 8th-most polluted city in the world Wednesday morning by IQAir with no other U.S. cities in the top 20.
